name: Red (1988)
description: Midway's last scheme, from 1986 to the airline's end in November 1991: a white upper body and a red lower body, the red's top edge level a little under the windows from the nose, with a thin dark pinstripe above it and a white gap between. Behind the wing the red and the pinstripe sweep up together across the aft body into the fin, running straight up parallel to its leading edge with white along the edge, so the fin is red with a white and dark-striped leading edge. On the fin a white mark: bars and a downward point reading as an M. 'Midway' in big red heavy italic letters just behind the front door, the windows showing through them. White nacelles with bare metal lips on the DC-9s, bare metal ones on the 737s; gray wings.

notes: Measured 2026-11-26 for ghost flights on DC-9-31 N901ML (October 1987, right side) on shapes/DC93.json, with the DC-9-15 (N1069T, 1988) and the 737-200 (N724ML 1989, N700ML 1988) measured as types. The DC-9s and the 737s wore the same layout: the photos show the red belly and the pinstripe on both. On the DC-9-30 the pinstripe runs at about −0.79 to −0.92 m (0.13 m) and the red starts about 0.34 m under it at −1.25 m; their heights read within about 0.1 m on three photos. On the fin the white along the leading edge, the pinstripe and the white gap run parallel to the leading edge; on the 737 they run on in the same straight line down across the aft body past the aft door, and on the DC-9s down behind the engine, where the turn to level is hidden (drawn as a turn of about 1.5 m radius under the nacelle). The bands are drawn parallel to the shape's leading edge at the widths read across them on the fin; on the 737 the photo's line sits a little aft of that low on the body. The fin's mark is our own simplified drawing; its place reads differently on different photos (center 0.29 to 0.36 up the fin), drawn between. The pinstripe reads dark brown to near black. The red reads from bright red to crimson. The scheme first appears on the 737-200s leased in 1986 (OY-MBW, July 1986) and was on the DC-9-30s by October 1986; some DC-9s still wore the Metrolink scheme into early 1987 (N902ML, January 1987). The MD-87s wore it too but aren't drawn (no MD-87 shape).

DC91.note: DC-9-15 N1069T (October 1988), left side, side-on: the title starts about 0.6 m behind the door and runs 7.15 m, as long as on the DC-9-30. The pinstripe and the red at the DC-9-30's heights (checked on the photo within about 0.1 m), the bands parallel to the DC-9-10's leading edge at the same widths, the mark at the DC-9-30's place.
